messages:
Maya Chen: Kicking off a quick bitsandbytes (bnb) / llm.int8 bakeoff on Llama-2-13b. Goal: measure quality delta vs FP16 across SQuAD/Winogender/codegen tests and collect throughput (p50/p95 tok/s) + GPU memory. Baseline = fp16.
Jorge Ramirez: Which bnb config? weight-only (load_in_8bit) + 8bit optimizers, or the new llm.int8 wrapper? Also do we use fp32 grads/accum?
Li Wei: Using bitsandbytes 0.41 + transformers 4.35. Running weight-only via `--load_in_8bit` and `--bnb-no-flash-attn` (for stability) — evals use deterministic seeds. Script: `scripts/evals/bnb_int8_bakeoff.sh`.
Priya Nair: I pushed the eval harness that runs SQuAD EM/F1, Winogender fairness probes, and a small codegen exact-match suite. It runs 3 decoding configs: greedy, temp0.2 sampling, and top-p=0.95. Use `--canonicalize` for code outputs.
Ben Thompson: Quick smoke numbers from my run earlier today (greedy): fp16 p50=280 tok/s, p95=120 tok/s, mem ~23GB. bnb int8 p50=560 tok/s, p95=240 tok/s, mem ~14GB. Quality: SQuAD EM -1.8 pts, F1 -1.2. Winogender delta +0.3 (within noise). Codegen EM drop ~3.4 pts (not great).
Maya Chen: Good throughput gains. Did you try `--no_split_modules` or forcing fp32 in specific layers? Any weird config diff in kv cache handling?
Jorge Ramirez: I tested sampling runs — int8 increases repetition for temp>=0.9, we see more degenerate outputs. Greedy is mostly fine. I can paste short examples later.
Li Wei: I also ran AWQ and GPTQ on the same subset: AWQ EM drop ~0.8 pts (better than bnb), GPTQ worse at ~2.6 pts. AWQ throughput was lower than bnb-int8 (~1.6x vs fp16) but quality was a bit better.
Priya Nair: Noted edge cases: codegen tests (function signature + docstring) show larger drops with int8, especially when the correct token is a long symbol — likely quantization noise on logits for rare tokens.
Ben Thompson: Ops suggestion: use bnb-int8 for latency-sensitive non-critical endpoints and fallback to fp16 for core QA/codegen. Also consider hybrid: int8 for prefix/embedding layers but fp16 for last-layer logits if that's feasible.
Maya Chen: Plan: canary bnb-int8 on a dedicated pool for the non-critical endpoints, then run a full 50-prompt eval sweep (all decoding configs). Who can create the canary pool?
Jorge Ramirez: I can spin it up: `infra create-dedicated --pool bnb-int8-canary --instance g5-4x --image rdinfer/bnb-int8:prod` — will tag it `canary/bnb-int8` and route 5% of traffic.
eval-bot: eval-bot: Quick automated sweep finished (10 prompts, deterministic): avg SQuAD EM drop 2.1, p95 latency improved 2.2x, sampling instability flagged for temp>=0.7. See /evals/runs/1769004321.
Maya Chen: :thumbsup: Thanks. Re-run with deterministic seeds across the full harness and post final numbers to the benchmark doc. We'll keep bnb-int8 as canary until codegen regressions are addressed.
